answer: An applicant locks a 65-credit bond and registers one juniper plot in a gale corridor, paying a premium rising with occupancy. Each gale claim carries a violet dye mark on damaged plants, matched by an auditor against plot registry and storm log; a reused mark, an out-of-corridor plot, or an out-of-storm claim burns the bond. The first premium costs 36 credits, the kth 36+5(k-1), the 1000th 5031; 1000 fakes pay 2,533,500 and lock 65,000. A rented-plot ring fails: one violet mark cannot serve two keys, and corridor fakes share its deductible. An honest applicant files one plot and one bond.
